description: Failures a composition can have that no constituent could have alone.

sources.name: imperial
sources.toml:
[registry]
schema_version = 1
name = "imperial"
version = "1"
[unit.ft]
dimension = "length"
factor = [381, 1250]
display = { long = "foot" }

sources.name: metric
sources.toml:
[registry]
schema_version = 1
name = "metric"
version = "1"
[unit.t]
dimension = "mass"
factor = [1000, 1]
prefixes = "si-engineering"
display = { long = "tonne" }

cases.rationale: THE case worth having. `imperial` defines `ft` (foot); `metric` makes `t` prefixable. Each loads perfectly alone. Together, femto+t collides with foot for the first time — a collision that exists only in the composition. Note that contested() reports NOTHING here: no symbol is defined twice, so this is not a definition contest and only the final load catches it.

sources.name: imperial
sources.toml:
[registry]
schema_version = 1

version = "1"
[unit.ft]

factor = [381, 1250]

factor = [1000, 1]

sources.name: deployment
sources.toml:
[registry]
schema_version = 1
name = "deployment"
version = "1"
[registry.prefix_collisions]
ft = "this deployment surveys land; femto-tonne is not a quantity anyone reports"

cases.rationale: How a composer resolves it: contribute their own source declaring prefix_collisions. A source defining no units is legal and exists for exactly this. Note `Gt` survives — narrowing the prefix set would have been the wrong fix, since emissions are reported in gigatonnes — while `femtotonne` becomes unresolvable, which is correct: its canonical form is `ft`, which now means foot.
Composition must never emit an unloadable registry: downstream has exactly one artifact and no fallback.
